newsitem.title: USA: Duke shuts Oconee S.C. units until mid-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Duke shuts Oconee S.C. units until mid-Nov.

text.p: Duke Power Co said Friday it plans to keep the three units at its Oconee nuclear power facility shut until mid-Nov to give engineers enough time to address safety concerns following an accident at one of the units last week.
The Oconee facility, in Seneca, S.C., has an overall generating capacity of 2,538 megawatts (MW), or 846 MW each.
Two of the units, numbers 1 and 2, are expected to resume power production in mid-November, said company spokesman Rick Zuercher.
The number 3 unit will enter an autumn maintenance program ahead of its original schedule, returning to service in mid-December, he said.
The outages were prompted by a mishap Sept 24 in which seven workers were scalded, four of them critically, when a steam pipe burst in the non-nuclear part of unit 2.
Oconee unit 1 was shut Friday morning, and Oconee 3 will be taken down Friday afternoon, Zuercher said.
Oconee 2 has been shut since the Sept 24 mishap.
"In our preliminary investigations we were not comfortable that the same pipe rupture couldn't occur in those units (numbers 1 and 3) as well," the spokesman said.
"We will again be doing an evaluation of the pipeline configurations," he said.
The Oconee outage may force Duke to purchase power on the open market to meet its supply needs.
"Typically we have a good margin of generation supply, but it could be that we may have to purchase power," Zuercher said.
Generation from several of Duke's hydroelectric facilities will be boosted to replace the lost Oconee output, he said.
Duke Power has a total generation capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which about 14 percent is made up by the Oconee station.
Oconee 3 was originally scheduled to be shut November 3 for a 50-day maintenance and refueling period.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
